status: implementation draft; not run by the author; not human-approved
deck_state: design/notice-deck.ja.json (Kimi K3.1 Pro) was read after the code was written. The schema matches the loader: all 18 required slots plus tax.body.2. There is no req.ref.path slot, so the plan literal is used. No text fit is claimed: the host runs --stills, and layout-report.json gives the measured sizes, ink boxes and overflow flags. A rough full-width count (chars x px) puts every line under its limit; the closest is role.files at about 31 x 34 px against 1420 px. This is an estimate, not a measurement.

copy_fit.rule: Body lines may step down from the planned size to 30 px, never lower. Row labels (30 px), kicker (30 px) and req.ref (30 px) don't shrink. Anything that still overflows is listed in layout-report.json flagged_for_kimi, and final mode refuses to encode. No Japanese is rewritten or authored here.
copy_fit.req.ref.path: Stays on one line after req.ref when it fits (lat 32 px SemiBold). If it doesn't, it splits verbatim at the last space into two 32 px lines ('github.com/studio-yebisu/ryoshu' / '(docs/REQUIREMENTS.md)'), moving under the lead-in if needed. It is never shrunk. A deck slot req.ref.path, if Kimi supplies one, takes precedence over the plan literal and is recorded as deck-sourced.

layout_adjustments_vs_plan: N1 row labels are baseline-aligned to the 40 px values (label y = row y + ascent(40) - ascent(30)). The plan gives only one y per row.
Markers, the N3 panel and text share each element's reveal (ease_out 0.45 s, rise 16 px, alpha x cards._fade). Markers rise with their row.

Markers are alpha-blended through an overlay. The base runtime card drew RGBA rectangles straight onto the frame, which replaces the pixel and ignores alpha, so the bar pops at full colour. Blending keeps the plan's 'subdued' fade.
tax.body.2 shares tax.body.1's 0.7 s reveal, as in the plan. If it is absent, the panel keeps the planned 270..560 size.

technical_corrections.finding: facts.json base_probe shows no color_space/primaries/transfer/range tags. The base encode piped rgb24 into ffmpeg -pix_fmt yuv420p with default swscale conversion.
technical_corrections.correction: Base color tags are copied only if present (none are). The notice clip is converted by the same ffmpeg default path inside the final graph, so the new cards match the base's untagged decode. Measured as background_continuity in notice.qc.json.

technical_corrections.finding: At 163.0-163.3 the base and the new render are the same bars, so they are highly correlated, and an equal-power law gives up to +3 dB at the midpoint. At 194.3-194.55 the pads carry different random phases (rng is drawn further in the extended timeline) while the plucks are identical, so the two are partially correlated.
technical_corrections.correction: Correlation-aware constant-power fade: weights (1-x, x) normalised by sqrt(wa^2 + wb^2 + 2*rho*wa*wb), with rho measured on the two signals in the window. This is equal-power at rho=0 and constant-amplitude at rho=1. The rho used is recorded.

technical_corrections.plan: click metric: edge max delta < 2x local median
technical_corrections.finding: For music, the maximum sample delta inside any window normally exceeds 2x the median, so this rule can fail even with no click.
technical_corrections.correction: Both are reported: the plan rule as computed, and the edge max delta (within 16 samples) against the maximum delta in the surrounding +-50 ms excluding the edge. Both are measured on the assembled PCM and on the decoded final AAC. Neither is asserted as a pass.

technical_corrections.finding: The decoded base audio could be offset from the synth timeline by encoder priming.
technical_corrections.correction: Lag is measured by cross-correlation over out 163.0-166.0 (identical bars) and applied only if |lag| < 1024 and the correlation is > 0.9. Otherwise it is set to 0 and recorded.

technical_corrections.note: synth() calls the same audio.py functions in the same order as make() (music, cues, sfx, the same normalisation, soft_limit), so it can also record the pre-normalisation peaks. Both the extended and the base timelines are synthesised. The plan's claim that the normalisation and bars 81-84 are unchanged is tested, not assumed: normalisation.*_equal and ext_vs_base_synth_163_170.max_abs_diff.

technical_corrections.finding: In audio.sfx(), the impact noise rng is drawn after all whooshes, so the two extra notice whooshes change the noise texture of every impact, including the base-timeline ones. Only the insert range of the new render is used, so preserved audio is unaffected. If the sfx peak changes, the insert SFX level shifts slightly and normalisation.sfx_peak_equal reports it.

measured_by_code_at_run_time: PSNR-Y/SSIM per frame on segments A and B (min/mean)
crossfade correlation/RMS, edge deltas (PCM and decoded AAC)
EBU R128 integrated loudness, output vs base
rendered copy first/last per displayed slot with deck sha256
